# Blueprint (Bryan Johnson's longevity protocol + supplement ecommerce)

URL: https://blueprint.bryanjohnson.com/

## Type system
- Display: `"DM Sans", sans-serif` — H1 45.6px/400, a modest hero size
  compared to most sites in this dataset (this is closer to a product/DTC
  ecommerce H1 than a clinic-marketing hero).
- Secondary display: `Montserrat, sans-serif` — H2 30px/500, used for
  section subheads, distinct from the DM Sans hero.
- Body: DM Sans 14px/500 (medium weight body text, slightly heavier than
  typical body copy, giving even paragraph text a confident presence).
- No serif, no mono.

## Color system
- bg: warm cream `#F6F4EC`, with a deeper cream `#F1ECDE` for alternating
  sections.
- text: deep navy `#111C35` / `#111B31` — a near-black blue rather than
  warm charcoal, giving the cream base a cooler, more "product label"
  feel than the terracotta-warm sites in this dataset.
- accent (CTA/interactive): saturated violet-blue `#5A31F4` — a distinctly
  unexpected, almost tech-startup purple against the cream/navy base;
  the boldest, most saturated single accent colour outside of Tally
  Health's magenta.
- Neutral grey `#C9C9C9`, `#4F4E4E` for secondary text/dividers.

## Layout & grid
- Structured much more like a supplement/ecommerce product page than a
  clinic or diagnostics marketing site — product photography, ingredient
  callouts, and protocol explainers dominate over lifestyle/clinical
  photography.
- Navy-on-cream palette with the violet CTA reserved strictly for
  buttons/links keeps the page from feeling like a typical
  wellness-brand pastel site.

## Sections (order observed, based on standard Blueprint page structure)
1. Hero: product/protocol statement, navy headline on cream, single violet
   CTA
2. Protocol/product explainer blocks (supplement stack, blood-panel
   results context)
3. Founder-credibility content tied to Bryan Johnson's own measured
   biomarkers (the entire brand premise is "my own protocol, my own
   data," making the founder himself the primary trust device)
4. Product grid (individual supplements sold à la carte and as a stack)
5. Footer with protocol/community links (tying back to the broader
   "Don't Die" movement ecosystem)

## Components/signature
- The violet-blue `#5A31F4` accent against navy-on-cream is a genuinely
  unusual colour choice for the wellness/longevity category — most
  competitors default to green, teal, or terracotta; this reads closer to
  a fintech or software-product accent, reinforcing Blueprint's
  positioning as an "engineered protocol" rather than a spa or clinic.
- DM Sans (hero) + Montserrat (subheads) is an unusual double-grotesk
  pairing — two geometric sans faces used for different hierarchy levels
  instead of the more common serif+sans pairing seen elsewhere in this
  dataset.

## Motion/interactions
- Standard ecommerce interaction patterns (product cards, add-to-cart);
  the brand's website is deliberately less "designed spectacle" than
  Superpower/Fountain Life/Tally Health, consistent with its positioning
  as data/protocol-first rather than experience-first.

## Biomarker/trust presentation
- Trust is founder-driven and quantified: Bryan Johnson's own measured
  biomarkers/organ ages are the brand's central proof point, discussed in
  long-form protocol content rather than shown as a dashboard on the
  homepage itself.
- No clinician advisory grid in the way Function Health or Prenuvo use one
  — credibility instead comes from the scale of self-experimentation and
  published protocol detail ("30 medical professionals," "best
  biomarkers in the world" claims), positioning the founder as the proof.

## What works
- Demonstrates that a longevity brand doesn't need spa/clinical visual
  cues at all — a navy/cream/violet ecommerce-product palette can carry a
  longevity brand that's fundamentally about a purchasable, systemized
  protocol (supplements, testing kits) rather than an in-person clinic
  experience.
- An unexpected, non-clinical accent colour (violet-blue rather than
  green/teal/terracotta) is an easy way to differentiate within an
  increasingly crowded "warm cream + one accent" category convention.

## Avoid
- The site's ecommerce-first structure and founder-centric trust model
  work specifically because of Bryan Johnson's public profile/notoriety —
  this pattern is harder to port to a brand without an already-famous
  founder; a generic "team" page would not carry the same weight.
- Be cautious of the broader brand's controversy (grift criticism, Amazon
  affiliate concerns cited in press) — borrow the visual system, not the
  trust-through-personal-brand strategy, for a fictional or B2B-safe
  design.

## How to apply
- Use a cool navy-on-cream base (not warm terracotta) with one unexpected
  saturated accent (violet, cobalt) to signal "engineered protocol"
  rather than "spa" within the longevity category.
- Structure the page as a product/ecommerce catalogue with protocol
  explainers, rather than a clinic-style membership/booking flow, when the
  offering is closer to a supplement or testing-kit product line.
